report.question: Developer request: bring the compiled donor’s dash into JUJUMP while retaining its timing and the platformer’s own physics. Recover a NEW standalone motion candidate. Prefer a compact experiment program to inspect the binary and chosen function bodies and run a checkpoint-bound controlled memory comparison. Choose hypotheses, code and inputs yourself. In a later model turn, use the actual result to choose evidence or a follow-up. Select inspected code and execution evidence, submit source, inspect real development first divergences and revise if needed. Use cooldown and remaining as the timer state field names for the current recipient instrumentation; infer their values and rules. Freeze a development-passed candidate and call separate acceptance, then conclude with actual experiment citations. The host checks the recipient only after recovery; you cannot claim recipient success. No pre-existing recovered implementation is available. Report incomplete work honestly; mapped fields, ABI, evaluators and recipient adapter are human assistance.
